title: Invesco QQQ Doesn't Own a Single Bank, and That's Not the Only Thing the Nasdaq-100 Leaves Out
author: Daniel Sparks
description: The Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ), which tracks the Nasdaq-100 index, excludes all financial companies and any stocks not primarily listed on Nasdaq. This means major banks like JPMorgan Chase and Wells Fargo, as well as NYSE-listed companies like Berkshire Hathaway, Visa, and Oracle, are absent from the fund. Despite missing the entire financial sector (11.5% of the S&P 500), QQQ has delivered superior long-term returns of 21% annually over 10 years compared to 13% for financial sector funds, though it underperformed in certain years like 2022 and 2024.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong 10-year annual returns of ~21% and 21% YTD gain in 2026 demonstrate solid performance despite sector exclusions. However, the fund's limitations are acknowledged.

title: Can American Express Turn AI Commerce Into a New Growth Driver?
author: Na
description: American Express introduced Intent Intelligence, a new framework that authenticates customer purchase instructions and spending limits for AI agents. Using Intent IDs and Proof of Intent Tokens, the system aims to enhance fraud prevention and streamline transactions. While competitors Mastercard and Visa are developing similar initiatives, AXP's dual role as card issuer and payment network provides competitive advantages, though commercial benefits remain uncertain.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: AXP is advancing its competitive position with innovative Intent Intelligence framework that addresses AI-driven commerce security. The initiative leverages its unique dual role as card issuer and payment network, potentially supporting payment volume growth and revenue expansion while reducing fraud costs.

Mastercard is developing a competitive Verifiable Intent framework with Google, demonstrating capability in the AI payments space. However, the article presents this as a competitive threat to AXP rather than highlighting Mastercard's advantages.

Visa is pursuing Intelligent Commerce initiatives and Trusted Agent Protocol to capture AI-driven payment volumes. While positioned as a competitor, the article does not provide specific advantages or disadvantages for Visa's approach.

Visa and Mastercard benefit from rising payment volumes and cross-border demand, PayPal is expanding through BNPL services and Venmo monetization, while Interactive Brokers and Robinhood are diversifying revenue through expanded product offerings. All five stocks carry a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating.

title: The Zacks Analyst Blog Highlights Walmart, Visa, Novo Nordisk, Village Super Market and Empire Petroleum
author: Zacks Investment Research
description: Zacks analysts reviewed five stocks on October 14, 2026. Walmart maintains strong fundamentals with solid omnichannel growth but faces margin pressures. Visa leads digital payments with momentum but elevated valuations and rising costs concern analysts. Novo Nordisk's semaglutide drugs drive growth despite competitive pressures and underperformance. Village Super Market outperforms its industry with steady growth and operational flexibility. Empire Petroleum struggles with liquidity constraints and declining production despite long-term growth potential.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong value positioning, integrated omnichannel model, healthy traffic and market-share gains, expanding revenue streams (e-commerce, marketplace, advertising). Outperformed industry by 1% over past year. Concerns about operating costs and margin expansion are offset by resilient fundamentals.

Strong scale and brand with broad momentum across payment solutions and outperformance of +12.6% vs. industry -6.5%. However, rising client incentives and marketing expenses are reducing profitability (adjusted net margin declined to 54.1%), elevated valuation, and regulatory risks warrant caution. Analysts assigned Neutral rating.

Semaglutide drugs (Wegovy, Ozempic) drive growth with label expansions and strong prescription numbers. However, significant underperformance of -29.6% vs. industry +30%, intensifying competition, pricing pressure, and higher spending cloud near-term outlook despite raised 2026 guidance.

Microcap significantly outperformed industry (+37.6% vs. +5.3%), with 3.7% revenue growth, strong operating cash flow of $108.8 million, and planned expansion. Trades at discount to peers. Concerns about margin pressure and unionized workforce are outweighed by operational strength and growth prospects.

Microcap underperformed industry by 58.8% (-14.9% vs. +43.9%). Faces persistent liquidity constraints, negative operating cash flow, declining production, elevated costs, and regulatory uncertainty. Long-term growth potential from Texas infrastructure and development projects cannot offset significant near-term operational and financial challenges.
